singleJudge.finding: [native] The tab labels are drawn larger in Title Case ('Installed', 'Updates'), while the artboard and the spec's tab tokens draw the navbar's 11 px uppercase labels ('INSTALLED', 'UPDATES').
[native] The group header 'DIRECT PACKAGES' uses the classic pane-header type (11 px, 700, uppercase) in this Modern UI capture, while the artboard draws 'Direct Packages' at 12 px, 600, capitalised.
[native] The select arrows are heavy browser-default chevrons, while the artboard draws a thin 16 px codicon chevron in both selects.
[native] The header line and the tab-strip line paint #313131, while the artboard draws both in the main panel's one divider colour, #2b2b2b (settings.headerBorder).
[native] The Vulnerable label badge has a small corner radius of about 4 px, while the Modern UI rule draws a label badge as a pill.
[native] Row authors are drawn at regular weight, while the artboard and the type rule emphasise the author or publisher at 11 px, 600.

[geometry] The settings and refresh glyphs sit 32 px apart centre to centre (ink x 865 to 879 and x 898 to 910), against 26 px in the spec (22 px boxes at x 868 and x 894, 4 px gap), so the gap between the two header actions is visibly wider than the redline.
[states] The details empty message is centred in the pane, where an empty state follows welcome-view content with left-aligned sentences and 20 px side padding.

[states] The author text of the Microsoft.Extensions preview row collapses to a bare "..." after the Verified mark, so that row shows no author, while the artboard's rows show a whole author and the row still has about 40 px of unused band to its right.
[geometry] The two details header rows are 6 px apart (Uninstall bottom y 133, Update top y 140), against the spec's 4 px (uninstall-button bottom 156.2, install-update-button top 160.2).

[states] The selected row's Uninstall glyph is a dim grey, clearly weaker than the bright foreground the artboard's row-action-uninstall draws on the selection band (spec token --nuiget-color-list-active-icon).
[states] The Dependencies framework groups carry counts as "(N)" text, unlike the surface's badges, and groups marked "(0)" still draw an expand chevron although they have nothing to expand.
[states] The selected row's author "James Newton-King" renders at regular weight where the artboard draws the author emphasis in semibold.

refuted.finding: The whole list column, tab strip and toolbar paint the side-bar background (#181818), while the artboard paints this region in the editor surface colour (#1f1f1f, the same as the details pane), so the panel reads as a side bar glued to an editor rather than one editor view.
refuted.reason: The crop does show the list column at #181818 against the artboard's #1f1f1f, but the cited rule's colour-role table assigns 'Side-bar surface (sidebar root, list pane)' to sideBar.background, so the capture follows DS-COLOR-1; the artboard's colour disagrees with that table, which the design-advisor may want to rule on.

refuted.finding: The Installed tab has a second, red-outlined badge "1" beside its count badge, an element the artboard's tab (one count badge) does not draw; it is a bare number that does not say what it counts.
refuted.reason: The red '1' is visible, but the interaction model specifies that 'the Installed tab also shows how many packages have known vulnerabilities', and the capture's project has one Vulnerable row while the artboard's has none, so this is a live-data difference that §6 excludes.

refuted.finding: The first six rows all read "Microsoft.Extensions...." because the names ellipsize at about x 270, with about 48 px of empty band to their right on rows that show no action, so at 1:1 the rows cannot be told apart; the artboard's names show whole.
refuted.reason: The crop does show six 'Microsoft.Extensions....' rows, but DS-ROW-5 expects the name to ellipsize with its full id in the tooltip and accessible name, hard 'DS-ROW-5: 15 rows, 8 names cut; badges clipped 0' holds, and the long ids are live content under §6.

refuted.finding: The Installed tab shows a second, unlabelled red-outlined count badge "1" beside "15", an element the artboard's installed-tab lacks, and it does not say what it counts.
refuted.reason: The red '1' is visible, but it follows the capture's data: this workspace has a vulnerable package and the artboard's sample shows none, and what it counts cannot be judged from the pixels.
